recipes.name: Taco Soup II
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: In a large Dutch oven, brown the beef and chopped onion over medium heat. Drain off any fat.
Add chilies, salt and pepper, beans, water, seasoning mixes, hominy, and stewed tomatoes to the beef and onion. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Top with shredded cheese, and serve with chips.

raw_recipe.headline: Taco Soup II
raw_recipe.description: This is a really good and easy recipe. Top with shredded cheese, and serve with chips.

video.description: This video shows you how to make a hearty, quick-and-easy taco soup. You’ll season ground beef and onions with taco seasoning and ranch dressing mix and then combine the flavorful beef with green chiles and hominy, plus three kinds of beans and stewed tomatoes. Top with shredded Cheddar cheese, chopped cilantro, sliced avocados, and sour cream.

review.reviewBody: Really, really good stuff!!! I substituted corn for the hominy and more kidney beans for the lima beans. I also added chopped fresh cilantro and sliced avocado on top - extremely tasty! The whole family liked this dinner so I will absolutely be making it again.

This is really good! It has a lot of sodium so I omitted the salt and all beans were no salt added and I rinsed them. It was not missed. It was perfect. I added 3 minced garlic cloves to the beef. Then put everything in the crockpot on low for 6 hours.This is great when you want a thick soup but are tired of chili.

Tasty as is and easy to modify. I've made this recipe or a variation thereof several times, both on the stove and in a slow cooker (about 4-5 hrs on low to let the flavors meld). Its really inexpensive, especially when I cut the meat in half, which makes it the best for feeding a lot of people, and it's great for a come-home-to lunch with friends on Sunday after Church.

I adjusted this recipe to suit our favorite ingredients and to make it a little lower in salt. I did not add the additional salt, I used three cans of organic black beans that I rinsed and drained instead of pinto-lima-kidney beans. I made my own taco seasoning mix and ranch dressing mix (sans salt) and instead of water, I used a low sodium beef broth. When I got all the ingredients mixed, the soup looked a bit thin to me so I threw in two 14 oz. cans tomato sauce and two cans drained and rinsed white corn. This was nice to come home to after a long afternoon and we enjoyed it. I'll make this again, with my changes.

The first time I made this it just seemed like chili. I made quite a few changes the second time around based on some reviews from here and my own ideas - admittedly, after my changes it's basically an entirely different recipe but wanted to share anyway: I omitted the kidney and lima beans and used black beans and corn instead. I also added one fresh chopped jalapeno and 3/4 of a can of Rotel diced tomatoes with green chiles in addition to the 4-oz can of green chiles. Lastly I added 3/4 of a block of Velveeta (pre-softened/melted in the microwave). The Velveeta made it a lot creamier and DELICIOUS! I actually forgot to add the salt, but I'm glad I did as the taco seasoning and Velveeta were salty enough. Topped with sour cream and Fritos...AMAZING!!!

i had to add in 4 cups of water total not 1 1/2 and i kept the extra salt out on the next batch and used low sodium taco mix... the original is very salty and almost like thick chili...my spoon stood up straight. once i changed some things very good and easy. i let cook on high for at least 2 hrs. my 7 yr old loves it too. requested it agian tonight! oh.. i also added in bell pepper and sub'd the hominy for corn.

REALLY GOOD!!!! Put it in the crockpot on high, till it started boiling. Then turned it down on low to simmer. Served it over corn chips, topped it with cheddar cheese and fat free sour cream. Delicious comfort food at its best!!!!!!

This is such an amazing recipe! I used ground turkey because it’s what I had and switched Lima beans for an extra can of pintos. This goes together easy but has tons of flavor even with the extra water I added because I wanted more broth. A+ for the ease of making and A+++ for flavor. Soooo good!!!!

A rainy, cold night in Atlanta required a hearty soup for dinner! I've made a vegetarian variation of this before but never used ground beef. This definitely added some depth. and flavor. 

Instead of hominy, I used a can of corn,....no lima beans, subbed chili beans, a bit of cumin and didn't add in the can of kidney beans. Served with sliced avocado, crushed pumpkin seed tortilla chips and shredded cheddar cheese. Delicious! 

The only downside is the browning of the beef and draining all that awful grease off and then blotting the beef to get rid of the fat. Doing this is not an option for us, it's mandatory. We can't and won't eliminate this step but it doesn't make for quick and easy prep! Always worth the effort when serving anything with ground beef as an ingredient, though.
This was really good. I used 2 14.5 oz cans of low sodium chicken broth instead of water and low sodium taco seasoning. I added corn and used a rotisserie chicken instead of beef. Yummy.
Used Rotel tomatoes instead of diced green chilie. Also used Mexicorn and made his entirely with ground turkey for less fat content. Delicious!
Really good
It's amazing

I left out the lima beans because they didn't seem to fit in a taco soup. The soup was plenty thick without them but you could replace them with black beans if you like a thicker soup. The only other change I made is that I used crushed tomatoes instead of stewed and that was for the hubs benefit. He doesn't mind tomato flavor but doesn't like them in big hunks for whatever reason. Overall good soup with lots of flavor and simple to make!
I used black beans instead of Lima beans — added garlic and sweet peppers— served with chips sour cream and cheese
I used whole kernel corn instead of hominy. I will definitely make this again.
Everyone enjoyed this. I will make it again. Exchanged fire roasted corn for hominy and butter beans for lima beans. Very easy and quick to throw together.
Our family loves this soup. The only change I make is I add a carton of vegetable broth and the consistency is just right.
Our family loves this soup. The only change I make is I add a carton of vegetable broth and the consistency is just right.

Love this recipe! I recently made a pot during one of our Colorado cyclone blizzard's and thank goodness I had this because we ended up hosting other family who had lost power at their place. I was so happy to be able to feed everyone. I never add the lima beans to mine, but I don't skimp on anything else, and it turns out amazing every time. I highly recommend. I serve with sliced avocado, corn tortilla chips, fresh cilantro, and sour cream on top. Sometimes I will cut up a lime and add a little lime wedge to my bowl. Thanks for sharing Julie!
